title: Transmission of Student Identifiers to Grading Service
description: The Grades Portal Web App (P1) transmits student id, course, file reference, and requesting role to the Assignment & Grading Service (P2). This flow inherently contains unique references to student identity, creating an identifier threat at the source of transmission.
assumptions: Student identifiers are transmitted in clear or insufficiently protected form during the P1→P2 flow.
uncertainty_note: Citation I.2.1.1 from context applies to identifier threats; confidence in mapping to this specific flow is moderate.

title: Processing of Identified Student Data
description: The Assignment & Grading Service (P2) receives and processes identified data including student id, course, and file reference. This constitutes processing of identified data as defined in threat tree node I.1.1.
assumptions: P2 processes the received data for grading purposes without additional anonymization or pseudonymization.
uncertainty_note: Citation I.1.1 from context applies to processing of identified data; confidence in mapping to this specific flow is moderate.

title: Non-repudiation of Grading Actions
description: The Assignment & Grading Service (P2) processes grading requests and submissions, creating evidence that could prevent individuals from denying their involvement in grading decisions or submission actions. This non-repudiation threat arises from the permanent record of who submitted what and when.
assumptions: Grading actions and submissions are logged with sufficient detail to prevent denial of involvement.
uncertainty_note: Non-repudiation context [4] indicates this is a threat (inability to deny), not a security goal. Confidence in Nr.1.1 node selection is based on general LINDDUN knowledge.

title: Processing of identified student submission data
description: The Grades Portal Web App processes student submission data that contains identifiable information about students. This processing occurs when teachers request and review submission queues, potentially exposing personally identifiable information.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of student submission data
description: Student submission data may be disclosed to unauthorized teachers or in an unauthorized manner. The system must ensure proper access controls to prevent teachers from viewing submissions outside their assigned courses.

title: Teacher impersonation during login
description: An attacker could impersonate a teacher during the login process to gain unauthorized access to student submissions. Weak authentication mechanisms could enable this threat.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Student Information
description: The teacher (EE3) may disclose student names, work content, or submission times to unauthorized parties (e.g., other students, colleagues, or external entities) beyond their legitimate role requirements, violating student privacy expectations.

title: Data Tampering by Teacher
description: The teacher may modify, alter, or falsify the displayed student submission data (work content, submission times) before or after viewing, compromising data integrity and potentially affecting academic records.

title: Linkability of Student Data
description: The teacher may link the displayed student submission data with other student information they have access to (e.g., grades, attendance, personal details), creating a comprehensive profile that exceeds the scope of this specific data flow.

title: Student Identifiability in Grade Records
description: Grade records contain student id, course, grade, feedback, grader id, and timestamp - all directly identifying information that can be used to uniquely identify students and link their academic performance across contexts.
assumptions: Grade records are accessible to authorized personnel and systems.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Grade Information
description: Grade records contain sensitive academic information (grades, feedback) that could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through improper access controls or data breaches.
assumptions: Access controls may not be properly implemented or enforced.

title: Linkability of Student Data Across Systems
description: Student id in grade records can be used to link this data with other student information systems (enrollment, attendance, financial aid), creating comprehensive student profiles that may exceed intended privacy boundaries.
assumptions: Student id is used as a common identifier across multiple educational systems.

title: Compliance with Data Protection Regulations
description: Grade records contain personal data subject to FERPA, GDPR, or other educational privacy regulations. Improper handling could result in regulatory non-compliance and legal consequences.
assumptions: Institution must comply with applicable data protection laws.

title: Processing of identified student grades data
description: The Grades Portal Web App processes the student's identified grades and feedback data, which contains personally identifiable information. This processing could expose the student's academic performance to unauthorized access or misuse.
assumptions: The system processes grades as identified personal data
uncertainty_note: Citation from context [5] I.1.1 applies to processing of identified data

title: Unauthorized disclosure of student grades
description: Student grades and feedback could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through improper access controls, data leaks, or insider threats within the Grades Portal Web App.
assumptions: Grades are sensitive personal data requiring protection
uncertainty_note: Standard threat for any system handling personal data

title: Linkability of student identity to grades
description: The student's identity could be linked to their grades data, potentially enabling profiling or tracking of academic performance across systems or time periods.
assumptions: Grades are associated with identifiable student information
uncertainty_note: Based on standard linkability concerns for personal data flows

title: Unauthorized disclosure of student grades during transmission
description: Grades and teacher feedback transmitted from the portal to the student could be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties if the communication channel is not properly secured.
assumptions: Network traffic is not encrypted or authentication mechanisms are weak
uncertainty_note: Using D.1.1 as a reasonable node for disclosure threats at flow level

title: Linkability of grades to student identity
description: The displayed grades and feedback could be linked to the student's identity, potentially enabling profiling or correlation with other data sources.
assumptions: Student identity is associated with the displayed grades
uncertainty_note: L.1.1 is a reasonable node for linkability threats at destination

title: Usurpation of student account access
description: If the student's credentials are compromised, an attacker could impersonate the student and access their grades and feedback, potentially misusing the information.
assumptions: Student account credentials are stored or transmitted insecurely
uncertainty_note: U.1.1 is a reasonable node for usurpation threats at external entity

title: Parent Account Impersonation
description: An attacker could impersonate a parent by exploiting weak authentication mechanisms to gain unauthorized access to another parent's child's grades.
assumptions: Authentication system has vulnerabilities or weak credentials

title: Unauthorized Grade Disclosure
description: Grades could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through system vulnerabilities, misconfigured access controls, or data leakage during transmission.
assumptions: System lacks proper access controls or encryption

title: Child Identity Exposure
description: The system may inadvertently reveal the child's identity to unauthorized users when displaying grades, potentially exposing sensitive personal information.
assumptions: System displays child identifiers without proper authorization checks

title: Grade Data Tampering
description: An attacker could modify grade records within the Grades Portal Web App, leading to falsified academic records.
assumptions: System lacks proper integrity controls and audit logging

title: Parent-Child Linkability
description: The system may link parent and child identities across multiple data points, potentially enabling profiling or unauthorized correlation of information.
assumptions: System stores and processes linked parent-child data without proper privacy safeguards

title: Unauthorized disclosure of grades and submission history
description: The Grades Portal Web App (P1) transmits sensitive student data (grades, feedback, submission history) to the Parent (EE2). This data could be intercepted or disclosed to unauthorized third parties during transmission or through system vulnerabilities, violating student privacy expectations.

title: Unauthorized access to student academic records
description: The portal may be accessible by unauthorized individuals who impersonate parents or exploit authentication weaknesses, gaining access to sensitive academic information about the child that should remain private.

title: Linkability of student data across systems
description: The grades, feedback, and submission history shared with the parent could be linked with other data sources (e.g., school records, other portals) to create a comprehensive profile of the student, potentially revealing patterns or sensitive information beyond the intended scope.

title: Potential regulatory non-compliance in data sharing
description: Sharing student grades and submission history with parents may violate data protection regulations (e.g., FERPA, GDPR) if proper consent mechanisms, data minimization, or security controls are not implemented, creating legal and compliance risks.
uncertainty_note: Regulatory requirements vary by jurisdiction; this is a general concern based on typical privacy frameworks.

title: Linkability of Administrative Actions to Personal Data
description: Administrator actions (creating/modifying accounts and parent-child links) could be linked to specific individuals' personal data across the system, potentially enabling profiling or tracking of administrative activities.
assumptions: System logs or audit trails exist that could correlate administrative actions with personal data records.
uncertainty_note: Tree node L.1.1 is a general linkability node; specific context may vary.

title: Identifiability of Students and Parents via Account Data
description: Administrator manages names, emails, and parent-child relationships - all directly identifiable personal information that could be exposed through the Grades Portal Web App.
assumptions: Personal data is stored in the system and accessible through the administrator interface.
uncertainty_note: Tree node I.1.1 is a general identifiability node; specific context may vary.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Sensitive Account and Relationship Data
description: Administrator has access to create, modify, and disable accounts and parent-child links, creating risk of accidental or intentional disclosure of sensitive personal data to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Administrator interface may have insufficient access controls or logging.
uncertainty_note: Tree node D.1.1 is a general disclosure node; specific context may vary.

title: Inappropriate Deletion or Modification of Account and Relationship Records
description: Administrator can disable accounts and modify parent-child relationships, creating risk of data loss or incorrect relationship data that could affect student records and family information.
assumptions: No adequate audit trail or confirmation mechanism for destructive operations.
uncertainty_note: Tree node Dd.1.1 is a general data deletion node; specific context may vary.

title: Unauthorized Access via Administrator Account Compromise
description: If administrator authentication is weak or compromised, unauthorized individuals could gain access to create, modify, or disable accounts and parent-child links.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms may not be sufficiently robust.
uncertainty_note: Tree node U.1.1 is a general usurpation node; specific context may vary.

title: Identification of Students and Family Members via Account Records
description: The grading service writes account records containing parent-child relationship links to the account directory. This data could be used to identify individual students and their family connections, potentially revealing sensitive personal information about family structures.
assumptions: Account records contain identifiable information about students and their family relationships

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Account Records
description: The grading service writes account records to the account directory. If the data store is not properly secured, sensitive student and family information could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through direct access or data exfiltration.
assumptions: The account directory may be accessible to unauthorized entities

title: Tampering with Account Records and Relationship Links
description: The grading service writes account records and parent-child relationship links. Malicious actors could potentially modify or corrupt this data, leading to incorrect family relationship mappings or fraudulent account modifications.
assumptions: The write operation is not adequately protected against unauthorized modification

title: Lack of Non-Repudiation for Record Writes
description: When the grading service writes account records to the directory, there may be insufficient audit logging or cryptographic signing to prevent denial of actions. This could lead to disputes about who created or modified specific records.
assumptions: Audit trails may be incomplete or not cryptographically secured

title: Explicit Data Disclosure to Third-Party Cloud Provider
description: Full grade records, assignments, and account directory are transferred to external cloud hosting provider EE5. This represents explicit disclosure of personal data across organizational boundary.
assumptions: Cloud hosting provider EE5 is a known third party with contractual obligations

title: Identifiability of Students via Grade Records and Account Directory
description: Grade records and account directory contain personally identifiable information that can identify individual students/users. Transfer to external entity increases identifiability risk.
assumptions: Grade records and account directory contain sufficient PII to identify individuals

title: Linkability of Disclosed Data Across Systems
description: Grade records, assignments, and account directory can be linked to identify individuals and potentially correlate with other data sources held by the cloud provider or other entities.
assumptions: Data elements can be correlated to create comprehensive profiles

title: Data Integrity During Transfer to Cloud Hosting
description: Full database backup and replication transfer to external cloud provider creates risk of data tampering, corruption, or unauthorized modification during transit or storage.
assumptions: Transfer mechanisms may not have adequate integrity controls

title: Usurpation of Data by Third-Party Cloud Provider
description: Cloud hosting provider EE5 may have unauthorized access to or misuse of the transferred personal data, including grade records and account directory information.
assumptions: Third party may not have adequate security controls or may breach contract

title: Regulatory Compliance Risk for Third-Party Data Transfer
description: Transfer of student grade records and account directory to external cloud provider may violate FERPA, GDPR, or other educational data privacy regulations if proper safeguards are not in place.
assumptions: Data transfer may not comply with applicable privacy regulations

title: Unauthorized disclosure of grade records
description: Grade records database may be accessed by unauthorized entities or processes, leading to disclosure of sensitive student, parent, and teacher information.
assumptions: Access controls on DS2 are not properly enforced; grading service P2 may have excessive privileges.

title: Student identification from grade records
description: Grade records contain personally identifiable information that could be used to identify specific students, parents, and teachers without proper authorization.
assumptions: Grade records include names, IDs, or other identifiers that can be linked to individuals.

title: Improper data handling in grading service
description: Assignment & Grading Service may mishandle or expose grade records during processing, leading to unauthorized disclosure of sensitive educational data.
assumptions: P2 lacks proper data protection measures; logs or error messages may leak sensitive information.

title: Regulatory compliance violations
description: Processing of grade records may violate FERPA, COPPA, or other educational privacy regulations if proper consent and data protection measures are not implemented.
assumptions: Educational data is subject to strict regulatory requirements; current implementation may not fully comply.
